title: Built a stock image platform for artists, designers and developers. Would love your thoughts on it.
author: prabhatpushp
selftext:
Hi everyone. I decided to build a stock image platform for artists, designers and developers. This platform is for getting inspiration and not your typical stock image website. I wanted to provide assets and images that users can use directly as a starting point. It can be later refined by AI or use it during conceptualization phase. Below are my design flow and architecture along with reasoning of choosing one over other.  
I am a next js developer but during making this platform I decided to go with astro as framework. My reasoning was SEO, performance and easy deployment. I was trying to keep the price as low as possible.

My Tech stack for now:

1. **Astro with SSR** (with **Cloudflare CDN** heavy caching as pages are mostly static)
2. **Cloudflare R2** with CDN (bcoz of pricing and unlimited egress bandwidth)
3. **PostgreSQL** (because of support for GIN indexing and vector support)
4. **VPS** (No managed provider to keep the costs as low and predictable as possible)

I am planning to add **Redis**, **imgproxy** Server, and **collaborative filtering based recommendation** in future. I am also planning to add login, bookmarks and other functionalities for image editing soon.

Currently I am beta testing and have only deployed approximately 30K images. I already have approximately 4M images generated across 15K categories. I am resolving the bugs and issues with the platforms.

My estimated final monthly costs: $180 for R2 + $30 for VPS server = $210

I would actually appreciate some **feedback**. Here is the link to the platform: [imagical.store](https://www.imagical.store/)

I am working on this project as a solo developer so please be kind and friendly.😅 I am open to **suggestions** and **constructive criticism**.

comments.author: fyrean
comments.body: Good job! I wonder since I dont see any features that would require server side, why not ditch the $30/month VPS + R2 entirely and just host the site as a static site on Cloudflare Pages? Completely free with no limits (except for max 25MB per file and 10k files limit (or 100k for Pro plan)

replies.author: prabhatpushp
replies.body:
at first I tried this approach of deploying on Cloudflare pages with web workers. But I found that prisma deployment on web worker is very tricky and you need to use prisma accelerate. To solve this I used prisma db platform to get accelerate connection strings but I very soon hit the 100K monthly limit during class A operations. Also the 100K worker requests per day was good but its calculation was vague. I was receiving 3-4K requests from unknown locations even without promoting the website anywhere. Apart from that I needed approximately 30gb postgresql db and the prices of hosted solutions was very high. Considering all these I decided to host on a dedicated VPS.   
Server side rendering is required bcoz I am planning to deploy approx 4M images and I cannot generate all these pages at build times otherwise the build process will be very high. R2 is for image storage. The total image size is around 10TB. So the cost is considering the class A and class B operations for R2.   
Would love to hear your thoughts on this.

replies.author: fyrean
replies.body: I see! Thats alotttt of images. Well I still think its insanely costly for you to stick with over $200 a month in server cost... Do you have a gameplan on how to at least fund the project in the short term? Why not drastically lower cost by self-hosting? A small computer connected to a 10TB drive (I recommend raid0 dual HDDs at least for twice the IO speed) will be much slower than R2 of course, but your cost would only be electricity and not $200, so like 200 times reduction... So yeah, why not selfhosting? Just hook up your server to cloudflared tunnel, it comes with SSL out of the box and you can run this in your home network no problem.

replies.author: prabhatpushp
replies.body: Actually the cost right now is not $200. It is the cost for full scale deployment. Currently I am beta testing with mostly free tier. My cost right now is under $10 per month. But I am planning for a full release soon. Home server option is good, would surely consider it in longer run. But for testing I think this is a nice setup. Thanks for the suggestions and your opinions.👍
